ai_guidance: The Office of the University Provost maintains a 'Teaching and learning with generative AI' resource hub with FAQs, sample syllabus language, and a self-paced course. ASU's posture is strongly adoption-oriented while requiring faculty to set explicit course-level rules.
enterprise_ai_tools: ChatGPT Edu (with GPT-5) free for all students, faculty, staff, and researchers from Oct 2025 through Sept 2026 under the expanded OpenAI partnership (FERPA-compliant); CreateAI Platform (ASU's in-house generative AI platform).
notable: First university to partner with OpenAI (announced January 18, 2024). AI Innovation Challenge has activated nearly 700 projects. Counterpoint: in April 2026, faculty objected to ASU's AI course-builder scraping Canvas course materials without faculty consent (Chronicle, Inside Higher Ed).
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion within a provost framework: faculty must clearly state allowable and prohibited GenAI uses in their syllabi.

lms: Canvas (recommended campus LMS; ~2,000 courses per quarter)
ai_guidance: The Stanford Teaching Commons publishes an AI teaching guide including 'Creating your course policy on AI'; the Office of Community Standards treats GenAI assistance analogously to assistance from another person under the Honor Code — not permitted to substantially complete an assignment absent instructor permission.
enterprise_ai_tools: Stanford AI Playground (multi-model platform: GPT, Gemini, Claude, Llama, DeepSeek, DALL-E 3) open to all affiliates; plus free Google Gemini, NotebookLM, and Microsoft Copilot Chat via SUNet ID (from Dec 2025).
notable: Home of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI), a major national AI-policy influence. AI Playground positioned as a 'safer AI platform' so the community can experiment without data leaving Stanford agreements.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion with an Honor Code default: absent a stated course policy, Community Standards' restrictive default applies.

lms: Canvas (Institute-wide since Fall 2020, replacing the homegrown Stellar system)
ai_guidance: MIT IS&T publishes 'Guidance for use of Generative AI tools' (data risk, vendor terms), while the Teaching + Learning Lab provides pedagogical guidance on GenAI in assignments and assessments, recommended by the Chair of the Faculty.
enterprise_ai_tools: OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise available to all MIT faculty via IS&T (approved for Medium Risk data); IS&T maintains a list of licensed GenAI tools; Microsoft Copilot Chat at MIT Sloan.
notable: MIT RAISE (Responsible AI for Social Empowerment and Education) — Institute-wide AI-literacy initiative whose Day of AI reached 170+ countries; Project NANDA's 2025 'GenAI Divide' report (~95% of enterprise GenAI pilots fail to show ROI) drew global attention.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion: no Institute-wide classroom mandate; instructors set subject-level policies.

lms: bCourses (Berkeley's branded Canvas instance, official since 2014)
ai_guidance: The Center for Teaching & Learning's 'Understanding GenAI and Campus Expectations' explains that campus leadership leaves GenAI adoption decisions to individual courses and faculty; the Office of Ethics, Risk, and Compliance publishes 'Appropriate Use of Generative AI Tools'; the Berkeley AI Hub centralizes tools and guidance.
enterprise_ai_tools: UC-licensed Google Gemini for all students (from Aug 2025, with negotiated data protections); Campus AI Sandbox beta (LibreChat-based multi-model access to ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, piloted March 2025).
notable: College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS) — Berkeley's first new college in 50+ years (2023); emphasizes UC-negotiated data protections rather than a single-vendor OpenAI-style deal.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion: campus leadership explicitly leaves GenAI permission decisions to individual instructors; unsanctioned use may constitute academic misconduct.

ai_guidance: HUIT's university-wide Generative AI Guidelines require Harvard-related GenAI use to occur through approved environments (the AI Sandbox or Harvard-linked enterprise accounts); the FAS Office of Undergraduate Education provides three model course approaches from 'maximally restrictive' to 'fully encouraging,' with no blanket policy.
enterprise_ai_tools: HUIT AI Sandbox — a secure, walled-off multi-LLM environment (Azure OpenAI GPT models, Anthropic Claude, Google models) approved for Medium Risk data; OpenAI enterprise accounts linked to HarvardKey.
notable: AI Sandbox piloted fall 2023, one of the first university-built secure multi-model GenAI environments; expanded as 'AI Sandbox 2.0' in 2024.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion within school-level frameworks: FAS offers three template policies; no university-wide blanket classroom rule.

lms: Canvas (centrally supported; instructors of organized courses must maintain a minimum Canvas presence)
ai_guidance: The Center for Teaching & Learning publishes a 'Generative AI in Teaching and Learning' resource suite recommending instructors decide whether GenAI fits their pedagogical aims and state policies clearly in syllabi; uncredited AI-generated work violates existing academic integrity policy.
enterprise_ai_tools: CIO-sanctioned secure AI tools (Aug 2025): Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Spark, UT Sage (UT-built AI tutoring platform), and Google Gemini.
notable: Declared 2024 the 'Year of AI' — campus-wide initiative including an online Master of Science in AI, an 'Essentials of AI' course open to all students, and the launch of UT Sage.
syllabus_policy_approach: Instructor discretion: three sample syllabus policy models (prohibited, conditional, permitted with citation); every instructor states their policy in a designated syllabus section.
